observations.seen: Flat, even daylight in frames 1-2 with little directional modeling. The character and house have weak key/fill separation. Frames 3-4 shift to a pink dusk grade that mutes the greens rather than adding a warm rim.
Contact shadows are barely visible: the character has no clear ground shadow in the grass. Trees and the windmill cast no readable shadow onto the meadow, so objects feel pasted on.
The lake is a flat pale blue plane with no sky reflection, specular glints or shoreline variation. The windmill's metal and wood show no environment response.
Distance haze on the far shore and treeline works in frame 4. A god-ray shaft by the windmill and faint floating motes appear. Fog in frames 1-2 is subtle but present.

Bush leaves use repeating polka-dot pink spots that read as a tiled texture. The grass has dithered, noisy alpha edges around the character. The roof tiles and the stone base of the windmill read well.
The low-poly faceted trees and cottage are charming. The character model is detailed and realistic, which clashes with the stylized world. The pink ghost-cat companion fits the style.

The character is small, about 8-10% of frame height, rather than the expected 18-25%. The character is buried in tall foliage at center. A large tree trunk crops the left edge awkwardly in frames 3-4.
The camera is a high third-person chase view, not side-on. Foreground grass occludes the character's legs. The framing drifts between shots, with the windmill cut off at the right.
Frames 3-4 have a heavy pink/desaturated grade that dulls the palette. Visible dithering/noise patterns appear around the character. There is no obvious bloom except on the companion glow.
The poses show a mid-stride crouch that looks stiff. Grass shows no visible bending around the player.
Clean rounded pill UI for the counter, controls hint, and Journal/Sound buttons. It is legible but generic. The HUD disappears in frames 3-4, and there is no gold coin accent.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
